A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Markovian CoT training work, with matching authors and retained arithmetic experiments. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 Sections 4.1–4.3 and appendices report original arithmetic training, CoT perturbation experiments, cross-model evaluation, and generated examples.

after.justification: v3 Sections 5.1–5.3 and appendices report original arithmetic and GSM8K results, optimizer comparisons, perturbation experiments, and cross-model evaluation.

M1.justification: The CoT bottleneck, frozen evaluator, and LoRA remain. However, v3 replaces v1's learned transformer value head with a historical-average reward baseline and specifies threshold-selected PG/PPO procedures alongside expert iteration (Sections 4.2–4.3). These substantially revise optimization. v3's inconsistent probability versus log-probability formulas do not establish a separate, definite reward change.

E1.justification: v3 retains synthetic fifteen-term addition and adds training and held-out evaluation on GSM8K mathematical word problems (Section 5.1 and Appendix C). This substantially extends the evaluated task requirements beyond bare summation.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 2 includes policy gradient and expert iteration as explicit quantitative comparators to PPO; v1 Figure 2 presents only the PPO training curve. v1 already reports qualitative trials of these optimizer families, so this is a bounded expansion of the reported comparison, not entirely new baseline families.

E3.justification: Arithmetic batch size and accumulation change from 8 and 15 to 6 and 8, and PPO clipping changes from 0.1 to 0.2. The CoT prompt also changes. v3 introduces GSM8K train/test evaluation with 80 CoT tokens, batch size 10, and 32 accumulation steps, plus answer-containment and sampled-answer accuracy measurements.

E4.justification: v1's multiple-severity perturbation sweeps for both Mistral and Llama are replaced by selected Mistral perturbations and unperturbed cross-model curves. v3 Figure 3 reports 10% truncation and 30% digit changes; its deletion label conflicts with the text's swapping description. Optimizer comparisons and qualitative examples are revised, while Gumbel-softmax, replay-buffer, and Claude abstract-compression analyses are omitted.

E5.justification: v1 shows smoothed curves and raw points without specifying repeated-run counts. v3 first specifies four runs per optimizer, using pointwise maxima in Figure 2 and four-run PPO averages in Figures 3–4. This adds run-count and aggregation information, without establishing an increase over v1's actual runs. Neither version provides between-run intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports GSM8K accuracy increasing from 24.64% to 35.71% within its experiment, an 11.07-percentage-point difference absent from v1. It also reports arithmetic answer containment up to 90%, average token log probability around -0.7, and new optimizer, perturbation, transfer, and qualitative results. Changed settings prevent treating the arithmetic curves as same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v3 replaces v1's Moore machines, wiring diagrams, fitness, and sender/self-truthfulness construction with a five-component Markovian language model and informativeness I(u,u',P). Its trajectory formulation uses a shared fixed predictor and a corresponding policy-gradient estimator. This substantially narrows and reformulates the mathematical framework rather than merely renaming notation.

C1.justification: v1 presents formal truthfulness and faithful reasoning as central contributions. v3 explicitly distinguishes measurable informativeness from faithfulness to internal causal reasoning, redefining the headline objective while retaining CoT dependence and transferability claims. Its abstract and contribution list also add the GSM8K performance claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving predictor formatting uncertainty, sensitivity to answer-bearing final CoT tokens, and improved pairwise-addition formatting. It also discusses serial-generation costs and the unverified applicability to general language modeling. Compression and steganography limitations largely persist, with the latter relocated to Appendix F.

D1.justification: The repository link, optimizer, learning rate, sampling temperature, and arithmetic token limits already appear in v1. v3 adds H100 hardware, LoRA alpha, gradient-norm clipping, and specific training/evaluation script and log locations in its reproducibility statement. v1's exact evaluator prompt is no longer supplied; external resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Turpin's unfaithfulness example, several mechanistic-interpretability references, and the GSM8K citation. References supporting the removed Moore-machine framework, including Niu and Spivak, Hopcroft, and Friston, disappear. The central comparisons with Scratchpad, Quiet-STaR, state-space models, and faithful-CoT methods remain, while the latent-knowledge discussion moves to Appendix D.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, formal exposition, and methods narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before the formal framework, lengthy exploration discussions become stepwise algorithm descriptions, and latent-knowledge and steganography discussions move into appendices. Ethics and reproducibility sections are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as question–CoT–answer and recurrent-state diagrams. Figure 2 becomes a two-panel optimizer comparison; perturbation plots are consolidated, and the Llama panels become a joint Mistral/Llama plot. A GSM8K figure is added, earlier supplementary perturbation plots disappear, and qualitative examples are reformatted as detailed logs.

improvement.justification: v3 better aligns its central claim with measurable informativeness and adds GSM8K evidence beyond v1's synthetic arithmetic. Clearer exposition and more specific reproducibility guidance improve usability. These gains are tempered by pointwise-best-of-four reporting without between-run uncertainty, conflicting reward and perturbation descriptions, and the still-unverified compression and human-interpretability arguments.
